newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Dadonghai A share offer priced at 3.20 yuan.
newsitem.headline: Dadonghai A share offer priced at 3.20 yuan.

text.p: Hainan Dadonghai Tourism Centre (Holdings) Co Ltd will launch an offer of 11 million A shares in the city of Sanya in Hainan province by the middle of this month, a company spokesman said on Monday.
The offer, approved by the China Securities Regulatory Commission, has been priced at 3.20 yuan per share, he told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
The official said Dadonghai had also received the CSRC's approval to list three million staff shares, issued at one yuan each in 1993, along with the A shares on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange.
Hainan Hong Kong & Macao International Trust and Investment Co will underwrite the A shares, he said.

The official said Dadonghai plans to use the proceeds from the A share offer to renovate and expand its four-star 238-room South China Sea Grand Hotel, which is being financed by money raised from its recent offer of 80 million B shares.
Dadonghai has total share capital of 320 million shares, including 101.07 million founder shares, 108.93 million legal person shares, 80 million B shares and 30 million internal staff shares.
The B shares, which were issued at HK$1.22 each, were listed in Shenzhen in October 1996.

In its B share prospectus, Dadonghai forecast net earnings of 63 million yuan for 1996 according to international accounting standards, compared with 39.90 million yuan in 1995 and 32.73 million yuan the previous year.
But the spokesman said Dadonghai now estimated net earnings for 1996 could reach 57.12 million yuan.
He said the company's operations were negatively affected by the unexpected closure of its two video game centres in Sanya in November 1996.
The official said Dadonghai closed down the centres to comply with the policy implemented by the Ministry of Public Security and Ministry of Culture. He gave no details.
Net earnings in the first quarter of 1996 totalled 9.33 million yuan, he said, but gave no comparative figures.
